seoTitle: Check Keyword Rankings in Semrush with Organic Research
metaDescription: Check a domain's keyword rankings in Semrush's Organic Research report, read the columns that matter, and know when to move to paid Position Tracking.
intro: Before setting up dedicated tracking for a handful of target keywords, it helps to see the full picture first: every keyword a domain already ranks for, its position, and how much traffic it pulls. Semrush's Organic Research tool does that from a single domain lookup, no keyword list required upfront. This guide covers getting from a plain domain search to a full ranking table, reading the columns that matter, and knowing when to move to ongoing Position Tracking.

steps.heading: Sign in to Semrush
steps.body: A quick search for "semrush" gets you to the official site fastest. Log in or sign up; ranking data needs an account, and the fuller reports need a paid plan (more on that below).

image.caption: A Google search for Semrush, with SEO Difficulty and other quick metrics already visible via a browser extension.

steps.heading: Enter your domain and land in the SEO toolkit
steps.body: Type your domain into Semrush's search bar to open its domain overview. You'll land on a dashboard with the full SEO toolkit sidebar on the left, covering Site Audit, Position Tracking, Domain Overview, Organic Research, and more, plus summary cards for Authority Score, referring domains, backlinks, and monthly visits. This overview is a useful gut check on the domain's overall strength before drilling into individual keywords.

image.caption: A domain's SEO toolkit overview, showing Authority Score, backlink counts, and monthly traffic alongside the full sidebar of tools.

steps.heading: Open Organic Research for the full keyword list
steps.body: Click Organic Research in the sidebar, under Competitive Research, to see every keyword the domain currently ranks for in Google's top 100 results. In a mid-size site this can run into the thousands, shown as a running total at the top of the report. It's the fastest way to answer "what am I ranking for right now" without knowing your keywords in advance. Semrush's own tool listings also refer to this report as Organic Rankings, so don't be thrown if a menu or an older screenshot uses that name instead.

image.caption: The Organic Rankings report, listing thousands of keywords with their position, traffic share, search volume, and ranking URL.

steps.heading: Read the Position, Volume, KD, and Intent columns
steps.body: Each row shows the keyword, its current ranking Position, the Traffic percentage it drives to the site, monthly search Volume, Keyword Difficulty (KD%), and an Intent tag (transactional, commercial, informational, or navigational). Together these tell you not just where you rank, but whether ranking higher is worth the effort. A keyword at position 78 with high volume and low KD is a far better target than one at position 1 with only a handful of monthly searches.

steps.heading: Sort and filter to find what matters
steps.body: Click any column header to sort. Sorting by Position ascending surfaces your strongest rankings first; sorting by Volume descending highlights your highest-opportunity keywords regardless of where they currently sit. Use the search and filter controls above the table to narrow to a specific keyword theme or URL when the full list is too broad to scan.

steps.heading: Move priority keywords into Position Tracking
steps.body: Organic Research is a snapshot, refreshed periodically instead of continuously, and it isn't built for watching day-to-day movement on a specific set of terms. Use the "Set up Tracking" option above the report to add priority keywords into Position Tracking, which monitors those terms over time, filterable by country and device. Both Organic Research and Position Tracking let you add competitor domains alongside your own, so you can see at a glance whether a keyword you're targeting is one a competitor already owns.

costNote: Viewing a small slice of a domain's rankings works on a free Semrush account, but the full Organic Research report and Position Tracking need a paid Pro plan or higher. Paid plans also cap how many rows you can pull in one export: 10,000 on Pro, rising through Guru to 50,000 on Business, per Semrush's own documentation.

faq.question: How often does Semrush update keyword rankings?
faq.answer: Organic Research refreshes on Semrush's own recrawl schedule, not continuously. Position Tracking updates on a schedule tied to your campaign, which can depend on your plan.

faq.question: Can I track rankings for specific countries or devices?
faq.answer: Yes. Position Tracking lets you filter and monitor rankings by country and device for location-specific results.

faq.question: Can I see how my competitors rank for the same keywords?
faq.answer: Yes. Both Organic Research and Position Tracking let you add competitor domains so you can compare their keyword positions against your own.

faq.question: Is Organic Research different from Position Tracking?
faq.answer: Yes. Organic Research shows a snapshot of everything a domain already ranks for, no setup required. Position Tracking monitors a specific list of keywords you choose, over time.

faq.question: Does checking rankings cost anything?
faq.answer: A free account can see a limited slice of a domain's rankings. Seeing the full Organic Research report or setting up Position Tracking needs a paid Pro plan or higher.

verifiedNote: Click path and screens come from a recorded walkthrough. Re-checked against Semrush's own knowledge base in September 2026: the sidebar section is Competitive Research (this guide previously said Competitive Analysis), the report is officially called Organic Research though Semrush's own materials also use the name Organic Rankings, and access to the full report requires a paid Pro plan or higher, which the original write-up didn't mention. The Intent column and the plan-based row caps were added for the same reason.
